title: Sprint Chisel: grooming + cutlist (Feb 2027)
content:
Goal: quickly reduce sprint scope for Feb27 release while preserving high-value UX improvements and critical ops fixes.

Context: backlog has swelled with several medium-priority UX polish items and platform requests tied to dedicated rollout metrics. We need a 'chisel' approach: remove surface-level polish and focus on three pillars this sprint — onboarding flow, route-level observability, and rollout safety nets.

Intake rubric (chisel rules):
- Keep: direct impact on new-user time-to-first-inference or mitigates production incident risk. (e.g., PROJ-3245)
- Defer: visual polish, micro-interactions, docs-only updates
- Kill: duplicate requests where existing feature covers 80% of need
- Quick win threshold: estimated <= 3 dev-days and no infra changes

Prioritization grid (quick sketch):
- Must: onboarding API key UX (CON-5621), route-level latency breakdown (CON-5589), fallback model policy toggles (CON-5637)
- Should: endpoint list reordering, bulk-delete by tag
- Nice-to-have: animation of empty-state, HUD microcopy refresh

Sprint cutlist (proposed):
- Cut entirely: "interactive tour" wireframe (low metrics lift), multi-column endpoint table (complex infra)
- Defer 50%: bulk-tagging refactor -> split into backend job + later frontend
- Keep but scope down: rollout canary dashboard -> initial static view + telemetry links, postpone A/B compare

Wireframe writeups (developer-focused notes):
- Onboarding API key UX: single-page modal. Steps: copy key, quick sample curl, live token-check button (POST /validate-key). Error states: 401 (bad key), rate-limit hint.
  Notes: reuse existing sample-snippet component; expose "open in playground" later as follow-up.

- Route-level latency breakdown: table with columns [route, p50, p95, p99, tokens/sec, error-rate]. Row-expander shows last 10 traces and last rollouts. Must paginate; keep default page size small (10).
  UX detail: use color-coded badges for p95 > SLO; allow quick filter "show regressed".

- Canary dashboard minimal: top row shows current traffic %, baseline model id, fallback enabled toggle (read-only for now). Below: time-series sparkline of throughput and error-rate. Interaction: clicking sparkline drills to traces view handled by observability team.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do we have telemetry endpoints ready for route-level tokens/sec? (ping infra)
- Can the token-check validation reuse hosted API sandbox keys? (security consult)
- Ownership: who will write acceptance tests for fallback toggles? (assigned to SE)

Dependencies & blockers:
- Infra: sampling endpoint for traces (INF-1198) currently in progress, due Feb 24
- SRE: new dashboard RBAC for customer-level views (SRE-403)

Next steps (this doc lifecycle):
- Thu 2027-02-17 grooming session to finalize cutlist (owners to bring estimates)
- Product to create PO tickets for scoped-keep items and annotate acceptance criteria
- Design to provide final modal microcopy by Feb 16

Notes to self (fast scribbles):
- Keep language terse in acceptance criteria. Avoid "nice-to-have" bleed into must.
- Consider adding a single "de-risk" checkbox in tickets to capture infra risk (helps cut decisions).

Appendix: quick links to related tickets and earlier cutlists for context.
